html:
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto led Pakistan from 1971 to 1977, as president and then prime minister. He was its most popular elected leader, and the army hanged him.

He was born in 1928 into a family of great landowners in Sindh and studied at Berkeley and Oxford. He became a minister at thirty under the military ruler Ayub Khan and, as foreign minister, turned Pakistan toward China. He broke with Ayub after the war of 1965.

In 1967 he founded the Pakistan People's Party with the promise of "bread, clothing and shelter". In the election of 1970 he won the west of the country, while Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won the east and an overall majority. Bhutto refused to sit in opposition, the army cracked down in the east, and Pakistan lost half the country (see the war of 1971).

He took over what was left. He brought home 93,000 prisoners of war by agreement with Indira Gandhi, gave Pakistan the constitution of 1973 that it still has, nationalised banks and industry, and began the nuclear weapons programme.

After a disputed election in 1977, the army chief he had himself promoted, Zia-ul-Haq, overthrew him. He was hanged in 1979 on a charge of ordering a murder. His daughter Benazir later became prime minister.
sum: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto led Pakistan from 1971 to 1977, as president and then prime minister. He was its most popular elected leader, and the army hanged him.
